verify:full.gate: every T0 + T1 + T2 task passes

verify:selftest.gate: every registered gate returns non-zero with one planted defect

ci:local.gate: HEAD, checked out into a temporary worktree and installed from the lockfile alone, passes every tier

audit:secrets.gate: 0 findings across every tracked and untracked-not-ignored file

typecheck.gate: 0 type errors across all 7 tsc projects

audit:integrity.gate: 0 unledgered markers, 0 non-ledgerable markers, 0 expired or stale ledger entries

audit:ratchet.gate: no regression in the cheap fields: suppressions, scan fingerprints, registered task list

audit:ratchet:full.gate: no regression in any measured field, including coverage denominators and the measured file set

build.gate: shared, server and client build with exit 0

test:unit.gate: all pass; shared and client coverage thresholds hold

test:integration.gate: all pass against a real mongod; server coverage thresholds hold

test:storage.gate: the storage port behaves the same against the real engine in a container as against the in-memory double the push tier uses: the shared StorageProvider contract passes unchanged, segments at the real 8 MiB framing size read back at exactly the offsets the framing predicts, an open upload carries a real initiation date, a missing bucket is named on every operation that can carry an error body so it reads as 503 rather than as a missing file, and the engine STORES a short middle part while the server refuses that same part through the real route and leaves nothing in the bucket

test:security.gate: the route table matches the real router stack, and every id-taking route refuses a non-owner without touching the target

test:observability.gate: no request value, audit row or production error body carries a secret, and a 5xx body is redacted to its status text

test:property.gate: every property holds in BOTH timezones: the crypto round-trip and its fresh IV, the five schemas as fixed points, combineExpiry across a fall-back DST repeated hour, the entropy metrics monotonic, deliveryNotes unrendered, and the folder forest acyclic and within the nesting cap under any sequence of operations

test:snapshot.gate: the Bitwarden JSON, Bitwarden CSV and Chrome/Edge CSV exports match their committed goldens byte for byte, every golden carries a provenance note naming its verifier, date and source, and import(export(items)) yields the same logical items

test:a11y.gate: every primary view and modal — thirty-three of them, in the real authenticated DOM, seven of them the document store's and one of them the isolated preview document itself — carries zero serious or critical axe violations, and the focus behaviours a scanner cannot infer still hold: the saved-address combobox keeps DOM focus on its input while aria-activedescendant tracks the active option, Escape closes that panel without closing the dialog around it, focus is re-homed across every billing-section transition, and the create dialog's focus trap holds

test:fuzz.gate: no import file and no backup document — arbitrary bytes, the committed corpus, or a generated hostile document — crashes a parser, exceeds its wall-clock budget, produces an item its own schema rejects, or loses a well-formed row to a swallowed duplicate key

test:resource.gate: every operation over a vault at MAX_ITEMS_PER_USER stays inside its committed time and memory budget: the backup collector refuses an oversized vault with 413 after mongod has delivered a fraction of it, the largest permitted backup still collects in full, a 10,000-item key rotation completes and one naming an unknown id changes nothing, a ~25 MiB backup whose escaped body exceeds 26 MB restores through the route's 30 MB parser, and both cross-user cleanup sweeps seek rather than scan; and, over an account at MAX_DOCUMENTS_PER_USER, a document at the operator's configured maximum size is delivered part by part without the server retaining a part, while a full document list is walked page by page with mongod delivering one page per request rather than the whole account

test:upgrade.gate: a vault and a .env written by the previous release are still readable by this one: every stored item opens under the crypto this release ships, decrypts to the bytes 0.7.0 sealed and parses to exactly what 0.7.0 parsed it to, no item schema declares a required field, a folder without sourceRefId and a refresh row without absoluteExpiresAt are accepted and the latter still slides by seven days, the settings that release lacked are filled in without a migration, that release's .env loads the current server's environment configuration in production, every variable since removed is ignored rather than fatal, and every required one that is absent or blank refuses the boot by name and fast

test:recovery.gate: this application survives the two disasters it is built for: a backup downloaded from one database restores into an empty account on a SECOND mongod with every item decrypting to the bytes that were sealed and each one still paired with its own name, the downloaded document survives the round trip its signature is computed over (so a signed backup still verifies, and an altered one does not), a backup is worthless without its backup password, and a real process killed mid-write always leaves the stored vault key OLD with its write fence still up — a login clearing that fence only once the dead rotation's lock has genuinely expired, the interrupted rotation completing on retry, and no crash before, inside or after the import write leaving a partial insert behind; and a crash in the document store leaves nothing the garbage collector cannot finish — an unrecorded part reclaimed only once its staging row is gone, an object neither collection names swept a day later, an interrupted purge finished and audited, and never a live document's object deleted

test:dst.gate: every test in all three packages passes in a timezone that observes daylight saving, not only in UTC: the whole suite is re-run under America/New_York, narrowing nothing, so a rendered date, a stored instant, an expiry countdown or a harness pin that is right only because local time and UTC happen to agree fails here rather than on a user's machine

test:flake.gate: the suite gives the same answer every time: ten complete runs of all three package suites, each in a DIFFERENT shuffled order derived from the one pinned seed and each with the file parallelism the push tier uses, plus the whole Playwright suite with three executions per test and retries pinned off, produce zero failures — and the number of runs and the number of failures are both recorded, because ten clean runs bound the per-run flake rate near one in ten rather than establishing zero

test:mutation.gate: the oracle: Stryker mutates every production file in the declared scope — packages/*/src/** minus the coverage-excluded entry points and the presentational UI primitives — and the suite kills at least the recorded share of them, with the seven core modules held to their own recorded scores, no file dropping out of the measured set, and no mutant left untested that was tested before

test:smoke.gate: the BUILT artifact boots in production mode against a real mongod, serves a deep-linked SPA route with a matching CSP nonce, and completes a register → sign-in → store → read-back journey whose ciphertext round-trips byte for byte

test:deploy.gate: the Compose stack comes up from nothing with every service healthy and both one-shots completed, publishes exactly one loopback-bound port and nothing else (the object storage engine none at all), completes a vault journey AND a document journey through that port — upload, byte-identical download, purge — serves the isolated render document from Express under its own tailored policy with the two opaque-origin headers scoped to its assets, keeps the data and the wrapped keys across a restart and a storage redeploy, refuses to boot on a half-rotated storage credential and boots on a fully rotated one, and re-runs its bootstrap without rewriting a rotated application password

coverage:check.gate: every package holds the line, branch and function coverage recorded in baseline.json, every production line this change touched is covered — with a dated COV-DIFF-EXEMPT ledger entry the only way to excuse one — and no changed production file sits outside the measured scope, where its patch coverage would read as 100% over nothing

audit:bundle.gate: the built client's initial payload and every emitted chunk stay inside their committed size budgets, so a library this application loads on demand — zxcvbn, Argon2id, the file-encryption tool — cannot become a static import without the build going red; both emitted documents (index.html, sandbox.html) and both asset directories (assets/, sandbox-assets/) are enumerated, and a missing document is reported as could-not-run rather than passed over

audit:deps.gate: 0 production advisories at moderate or above

audit:secrets:full.gate: 0 findings across the working tree AND every blob in git history

deadcode.gate: 0 unused files, exports, types or dependencies; duplication at or below the committed ceiling

audit:config.gate: 0 error-level findings from actionlint, hadolint and spectral

audit:openapi.gate: the HTTP contract the server generates carries no breaking change against the committed snapshot of the last release it describes, unless the root package.json MAJOR has been raised in the same commit

audit:licenses.gate: every production dependency carries an allowlisted licence; 0 copyleft

test:e2e.gate: every Playwright spec passes, against a harness that starts an in-memory MongoDB AND the pinned object-storage engine in a container, so the document journeys run against the engine the stack ships rather than against a double — Chromium over every spec, and a second Firefox project over the clipboard-hygiene and auto-lock specs, whose answers depend on the browser's clipboard-activation and visibility rules rather than on this application

audit:image.gate: all 4 images build; nginx -t passes; compose config resolves; 0 fixable HIGH/CRITICAL

gaps.detail: `test:mutation` is registered but has no `mutation` block in baseline.json, so it holds no floor, exits 1 by design, and `npm run verify:full` does not pass. The tier-0 and tier-1 surface that the pre-push hook and the release workflow run is unaffected. Two of three legs are measured but unbanked, because they ran while another project saturated the machine and a CPU-starved timeout is recorded as a kill.

playwright.config.ts now declares two engine projects: Chromium over every spec, and Firefox over the two whose answers depend on the engine (clipboard-hygiene, auto-lock), attributed in the JUnit report by project name. That leg drives a GENUINE transient-activation refusal on Gecko and the gesture-scoped retry that follows it, so the clipboard guard is no longer verified only by unit tests with simulated refusals. What is still asserted about one engine only: WebKit, and the other nineteen specs — the latter deliberately, because they assert application behaviour that does not vary by engine.

No benchmark, load, stress, spike or soak testing. `test:resource` holds nine measured scenarios to committed time and memory ceilings — seven over a 10,000-item vault (`RESOURCE_SCENARIOS` in `scripts/ci/lib/resource-budgets.mjs` is the list), plus a document at the configured maximum size delivered part by part and a document list walked at MAX_DOCUMENTS_PER_USER — but its noise band is 2.4-50 percent (SUP-0027), so it sees a step change and nothing smaller. There is no concurrent-user SLO for a single-tenant self-hosted deployment to test against.

No DAST pass. The classes a baseline scan finds are covered statically and by direct assertion — security headers and CSP per response, the cross-user authorization matrix over every id-taking route, a CSRF suite, and the CodeQL security-and-quality suite over the source — but nothing probes the running stack from outside. The target already exists: `test:deploy` stands the whole Compose stack up.

No SBOM is produced or published. The dependency surface is gated three ways (`audit:deps` advisories, `audit:licenses` allowlist, Trivy over all three images), but none of them emits a bill of materials a downstream consumer could read.

No visual-regression baseline and no deliberate latency injection. Function is covered by axe over thirty-three views, the component suites and the E2E journeys; the offline path is covered by the IndexedDB cache and service-worker tests.

No chaos testing. The topology offers little surface — one datastore, no service mesh, no inter-service RPC to sever — and the failure modes that do exist are driven directly by `test:recovery`, which SIGKILLs a real process at eight injection points.

Node 24 is pinned in .nvmrc, in engines.node and in every image, so no supported matrix exists to test across; the dropped Node 22 leg is recorded in the README as a known gap on the same grounds. The Windows leg cannot run on the maintainer's machine.

`test:a11y` blocks on axe impacts `critical` and `serious` only; `moderate` findings are reported but deliberately NOT ratcheted (`ratchet-check.mjs` records only `a11y.critical`, `a11y.serious` and `a11y.viewsScanned`), and the ones currently open across the thirty-three scanned views are `landmark-one-main`, `page-has-heading-one`, `region`, `landmark-unique` and `heading-order` (the count is in `a11y.json`, and is deliberately not repeated here: nothing would keep it true). The scan also runs in the light theme only.

gaps.area: the isolated render document under the production header set
gaps.detail: No gate RENDERS `/sandbox.html` in a browser under the headers a deployment actually sends. The E2E and accessibility suites drive the Vite dev server, which has neither helmet nor the stack's Nginx, so the tailored per-response policy and the two CORS-ish headers scoped to `sandbox-assets/` are absent there; `test:deploy` and `test:smoke` assert those headers over HTTP, directive by directive against the server's own exported constant, but neither runs a browser. What stands in for it is the pair: the behavioural assertions in the E2E viewer specs (a real `/sandbox.html` rendering a real document, including the hostile-input corpus) plus the header assertions in those two gates. The residual risk is a policy that is correct on the wire and still breaks a renderer in a real engine — a `blob:` media source or a `data:` image refused by a browser rule no HTTP assertion can see. Closing it needs a Playwright project pointed at the built artifact behind the stack's own Nginx rather than at the dev server. No suppression is attached because nothing is excused: this is a stated boundary of what the gate surface covers.

deferred.test:api: No separable command exists today. Every supertest suite lives beside the unit suites in packages/server/tests/*.test.ts, so the only ways to register it would be a committed test filter (a non-ledgerable TEST-FILTER under the integrity doctrine) or a second, duplicate invocation of the 125-second server suite that would report false independence. test:integration runs those suites today. Register test:api once the API suites move under their own directory.
